readings: Linking driver standings to races by race id (and dropping standings with no matching race), work out for each race name (`races.name`) the average season-to-date championship points (`driverStandings.points`, ignoring missing values) and the number of distinct drivers (`driverId`) with standings under that name. Take the average of that count across all race names, and keep only the race names whose count is strictly above it. Return a single row with three values: the average of those race names' average points, the average of their counts, and the average amount by which their count exceeds the overall average count. Don't round anything.
queries:
WITH per_name AS (
  SELECT r.name AS name,
         AVG(ds.points) AS avg_points,
         COUNT(DISTINCT ds.driverId) AS cnt
  FROM driverStandings ds
  JOIN races r ON ds.raceId = r.raceId
  GROUP BY r.name
),
overall AS (
  SELECT AVG(cnt) AS avg_cnt FROM per_name
)
SELECT AVG(p.avg_points) AS avg_of_avg_points,
       AVG(p.cnt) AS avg_cnt,
       AVG(p.cnt - o.avg_cnt) AS avg_excess
FROM per_name p
CROSS JOIN overall o
WHERE p.cnt > o.avg_cnt;
